title: hiring
subtitle: Verify any recruiter in seconds. Companies publish a domain-rooted declaration; candidates check it independently. No signup, no data collection — everything runs in your browser.

whatIs.title: What is hiring.txt?
whatIs.description: A simple text file at /.well-known/hiring.txt that declares a company's legitimate recruiting channels, domains, and commitments. Like robots.txt for search engines or security.txt for vulnerability disclosure — but for protecting job seekers from recruitment fraud.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.stat2Label: people exposed to fake job offers yearly
problem.description: Scammers impersonate real companies, use lookalike domains, and exploit the opacity of hiring processes. Candidates have no reliable way to verify if a recruiter is legitimate.

solution.title: The Solution
solution.step1Desc: Place a hiring.txt file on your domain declaring official channels, application URLs, and Never commitments.
solution.step2Desc: Paste the recruiter's email, link, or message into our verifier. We fetch hiring.txt from the company's domain and cross-reference.
solution.step3Desc: VERIFIED, UNKNOWN, or SUSPICIOUS — with clear reasoning and actionable next steps. No account needed.

openProtocol.title: Open Protocol
openProtocol.description: hiring.txt is not a product — it's a convention. Like robots.txt, anyone can implement it. HireGuard provides the tools and reference implementation.
